A Tamagotchi-Style Game for Interactive Thyroid
Cancer Care and Education
Thiago Narak C. de Oliveira
CCT & GIRA Lab
Universidade de Fortaleza
Fortaleza-CE, Brasil
narak@unifor.br
Juliana Amaral de Figueiredo
CCT
Universidade de Fortaleza
Fortaleza-CE, Brasil
jup.amaral77@gmail.com
Maria Andr´eia Formico Rodrigues
PPGIA & GIRA Lab
Universidade de Fortaleza
Fortaleza-CE, Brasil
andreia.formico@gmail.com
Abstract—This work introduces a serious game aimed at
enhancing awareness and management of thyroid cancer through
gamified learning. It innovates by personifying the thyroid gland
into a virtual pet within a Tamagotchi-style game framework. The
interactive virtual thyroid comes with different health problems,
visual adornments, genders, and age options, all of which are
randomly assigned by the game system to personalize the
experience. This design aspect enriches the player’s engagement
by presenting a variety of scenarios and challenges, enhancing the
educational value. Players engage in comprehensive care for their
virtual thyroid pet, encompassing health monitoring, treatment
decision-making, and overall well-being maintenance. This ap-
proach not only narrows the gap between digital entertainment
and health education but also introduces a novel channel for
disseminating information about thyroid cancer and promoting
a ludic understanding of thyroid health management strategies.
Furthermore, the game was playtested with thyroid health
specialists, resulting in qualitative feedback that underscores the
game’s potential as a useful educational tool in the field.

I. INTRODUCTION
Thyroid cancer remains one of the most common cancers
globally [1]. The latest estimates from the American Cancer
Society in the United States for 2024 indicate approximately
44,020 new cases (12,500 among men and 31,520 among
women), with around 2,170 fatalities attributed to the disease
(990 men and 1,180 women) [2], indicating a continuing rise
in its global prevalence [3]. Notably, thyroid cancer tends
to be diagnosed at a younger age compared to most other
adult cancers, with the average diagnosis age being 51. The
incidence is three times higher in women than in men [2].
Differentiated thyroid cancer, the most prevalent subtype,
typically responds effectively to standard treatments, including
radioactive iodine therapy, among other types of treatment [4].
Tamagotchi-style-based applications can offer a creative and
engaging approach to exploring health issues, such as in the
development of games centered around cancer. The concept
of virtual pets, pioneered by Bandai’s Tamagotchi in 1996
[5], introduced an interactive platform where players engage
in nurturing a digital creature through its lifecycle, mirroring
the natural progression from birth to death. This innovative

approach not only captured the imagination of children but
also expanded its appeal across ages, engaging teenagers and
adults in the virtual care of their digital companions. The
Tamagotchi phenomenon, originating from Japan, showcases
the evolution of virtual pets from simple pixelated figures on
a 16x16 display to complex characters within the immersive
worlds of later versions like My Tamagotchi Forever [6].
These advanced iterations incorporate leveling systems, 3D
mini-games, and high-quality graphics, broadening the scope
of interaction and care strategies—ranging from feeding and
hygiene to medical attention and emotional support—essential
for the pet’s survival and well-being.
The development of serious games and health applications
highlights their essential role in healthcare education and
engagement [7], [8]. Simulating real-life health management
scenarios, these tools create a dynamic and immersive environ-
ment that boosts the understanding and retention of informa-
tion [9]. Moreover, they connect traditional health education
with the digital era, appealing to diverse learning preferences.
This approach also helps to deepen health issue comprehension
and promote proactive health management, encouraging users
to better understand and participate in their health care [10].
This work introduces CancerST, a serious game designed
to enhance thyroid cancer awareness and management through
gamified learning. Leveraging the mechanics of care and
engagement found in traditional Tamagotchi-style games, Can-
cerST innovatively personifies the thyroid gland, transforming
it into an interactive virtual pet with different health problems,
visual adornments, gender, and age options, all of which
are randomly assigned by the game system to personalize
the experience. This feature enhances player engagement by
introducing varied scenarios and challenges, increasing the
game’s educational value. Players are responsible for their
virtual thyroid’s comprehensive care, including health moni-
toring, treatment decisions, and well-being maintenance. This
approach merges gaming with health education, offering a
new way to learn about thyroid cancer and understand health
management strategies. Through this synthesis, we aim to
improve awareness and educate players about managing this
increasingly common disease through interactive gameplay.

II. RELATED WORK
Although the authors did not find serious games for thyroid
cancer awareness or management in the academic literature
reviewed, the emphasis on technological advancements and
targeted therapies indicates significant interest. Discussions
on the National Cancer Institute’s website [11] further high-
light the potential of technology to improve thyroid cancer
management and awareness. This source highlights ongoing
research into several forms of thyroid cancer, including a com-
prehensive understanding of the current landscape in treatment
advancements and the significant interest in leveraging tech-
nology and digital tools for better patient outcomes. Reviewing
these studies and advancements in treatment provided valuable
insights for our game. Furthermore, these findings indicate a
research gap in serious games for thyroid cancer, pointing
out an opportunity to create and assess educational games
in this field. This opens the door for a more comprehensive
exploration of thyroid cancer research and the possible contri-
butions of educational technology. This exploration directs us
toward virtual pet games, a field ripe for applying educational
strategies via gaming technologies.
For example, Om Nom: Merge [12], developed by Zeptolab
and launched globally in November 2019, offers a colorful,
casual gaming experience centered on merging characters to
progress. Featuring 3D isometric gameplay, it invites players
to earn rewards by merging and feeding pets from level 1,
simplifying gameplay with a focus on collection and progres-
sion. This resource allows for the creation of superior pets and
enhanced earnings, with an incubator for new species and a
nursery for breeding unique abilities, aiming to streamline the
casual experience through pet merging for discoveries.
Transitioning from Om Nom: Merge to Pou [13] marks
a shift towards nurturing a digital pet. Pou engages players
in caring for their pet, offering customization options for
appearance and surroundings. Unlike Tamagotchi, Pou avoids
permanent consequences, such as death, and instead reflects
neglect through changes in its appearance. This design choice
prioritizes care and interaction, with various contexts including
health treatments and mini-games.
Further diversifying the virtual pet landscape, Pixel Petz
[14] by Minidragon harnesses 2D-pixel art to enable users
to create, collect, breed, and trade unique virtual pets within
a community-driven platform. Emphasizing customization, it
caters to both canine and feline enthusiasts with a breeding
system for offspring and customizable clothing for pets. This
game encourages players to manage multiple pets’ hygiene,
hydration, and nutrition, enriching the pet care experience with
interactive care elements.
Advancing the genre, My Talking Tom 2 [15] focuses on the
comprehensive care of Tom, a kitten with a range of needs
from happiness to hygiene, presented through a 2D display.
It combines cleaning, feeding, and bedtime routines with
interactive elements to ensure Tom’s well-being, integrating
a wardrobe system for customization and several mini-games
to boost happiness. This blend of entertainment and pet care
responsibility lessons echoes the engaging mechanics found in
the previously mentioned games.
The noted absence of academic literature addressing serious
games for thyroid cancer awareness and management under-
scores the significance of developing our game. This literature
gap highlights an opportunity for innovative educational tools
in this domain. Moreover, the success and engagement ob-
served in virtual pet games like Om Nom: Merge, Pou, Pixel
Petz, and My Talking Tom 2 pave a promising path for health
education and awareness. These games successfully combine
entertainment with the nuances of pet care, suggesting a
potential for leveraging similar mechanics even in distinct
areas such as thyroid cancer awareness and education. Draw-
ing inspiration from these popular titles, which incorporate
nurturing, monitoring, and interactive learning in a virtual
setting, CancerST aims to offer a new way to educate players
about thyroid cancer management and care. This innovative
approach, which personifies the thyroid gland as a virtual pet,
not only promises to engage users in a familiar gameplay
format but also educates them on the important aspects of
thyroid health, potential treatments, and the importance of
ongoing management.
III. MOST COMMON THYROID DISEASES
In the context of developing serious games for health
education, particularly those focused on thyroid health, it
is important to integrate accurate medical information into
gameplay to enhance learning outcomes. The primary thyroid
conditions that can be featured include hypothyroidism, hy-
perthyroidism, and thyroid cancer [16], [17], each presenting
unique challenges and learning opportunities for players.
Hypothyroidism involves an underactive thyroid gland
failing to produce sufficient hormones, leading to symptoms
that could be gamified into scenarios where players must
manage energy levels, mood, and metabolism within the game
environment to maintain their character’s health. It is typically
treated with daily thyroid hormone replacement medication to
normalize hormone levels.
Hyperthyroidism is an overactivity of the thyroid gland.
Treatment strategies include antithyroid medications to reduce
thyroid hormone production, radioactive iodine therapy to
ablate thyroid tissue and surgical removal of the gland in more
resistant cases. It could be translated into gameplay elements
that require players to balance excessive energy or manage
anxiety within their characters, simulating real-life symptom
management.
Thyroid Cancer, being more complex, offers a pathway for
game developers to incorporate treatment options (radioactive
iodine therapy, surgery, and radiotherapy), and post-treatment
and post-operative care into the game narrative, educating
players on the signs of thyroid nodules, the importance of early
detection, and the steps involved in treatment and recovery.
Although surgical removal of the thyroid is one of the cancer
treatments, this modeling was left in our game for future work.
Nodules are growths that can appear on the thyroid, poten-

tially requiring a spectrum of treatments from observation to

thyroid hormone therapy and even surgical removal, depending
on the nodule’s nature and impact on thyroid function.
For computer game scientists, centering on these conditions
involves crafting an engaging, informative experience that
faithfully portrays the challenges and management tactics
linked to thyroid diseases. This method not only aids in public
health education, but also in early disease detection, and pa-
tient empowerment through interactive and immersive learning
environments. Merging medical expertise with game design
offers developers a chance to produce impactful tools that
extend beyond entertainment, serving as valuable resources
in health education and awareness.
IV. GAME OVERVIEW
In developing CancerST, we drew inspiration from other
cancer and mental health-themed games we have created
[18], [19], [20], [21], [22], and from medical collaborations
with cancer specialists, adhering to the highest design and
programming standards. We employ methodologies like iter-
ative development and responsive design [23] and integrate
player-centric game mechanics as Schell describes [24]. These
practices guarantee that the game is both technically sound and
engaging for players.
Developed using the Unity engine for its robust game
development features, our game features original art created in
Adobe Photoshop and animations produced with Unity. This
approach ensures high-quality visuals and a distinctive artistic
style, with the background of the opening scene displaying
various thyroid characters affected by typical diseases, em-
phasizing thyroid care and its vulnerability to cancer and other
health issues (Fig. 1).
The game highlights the thyroid’s role in regulating bodily
functions and the need for special attention such as sleeping,
exercise, healthy eating, and care to prevent illness. The
player’s mission is to provide the best care for each thyroid
character on screen, choosing between personal and medical
care as needed. The soundtrack was crafted by customizing
a lullaby audio freely available [25], slowing it down to
better suit the game’s atmosphere. This blend of original
gameplay, animations, audio, and art establishes a gaming
environment that is not only user-friendly but also enriches the
player’s learning experience, aligning with the serious game’s
educational objectives in the healthcare domain.
A. Art & Game Design
The game’s art & design use a color palette derived from the
ribbon representing thyroid cancer for its interface and menus,
both in-game and out-of-game. The main character is the thy-
roid gland itself, depicted in diverse health conditions: healthy,
affected by hypothyroidism, experiencing hyperthyroidism,
undergoing cancer (showcasing varied tumor sizes), following
partial surgery (either left or right side removed), or after
complete removal (showcasing only the trachea). This creative
approach not only serves to educate players about the physical
aspects of thyroid conditions and treatments but also immerses
them in the journey of thyroid health management through a
Fig. 1. Opening scene of CancerST.
visually engaging experience. In particular, the authors drew
inspiration for developing this serious game based on their own
and familial experiences, including hypothyroidism, surgery,
and treatment with radioactive iodine therapy. None of the
inspirations for the game suggested that the protagonist, even
when depicted as afflicted, should be unfriendly. Instead,
reflecting the high curability rate of early-diagnosed thyroid
cancer, the character is designed to be approachable and
friendly.
In CancerST, basic care options for the thyroid character
are displayed as buttons on the left and right sides of the
game home screen (Fig. 2), utilizing a 2D point-and-click
interface that is complemented by a wide array of animations.
Interactions enable players to touch buttons, triggering actions
within the game’s internal system to advance gameplay flow.
When a button is activated, all other buttons on the game
home become inactive during the animation to prevent action
queuing or overlapping. This intuitive design allows players to
easily access and engage with the care routines necessary for
managing the health of the thyroid, enhancing the educational
aspect of the game through direct interaction.
Fig. 2. Game home of CancerST, with a thyroid character with cancer.
More specifically, personal care buttons are equipped with
square colliders on top of the interaction button sprites. A
RayCast system is utilized for button selection. When a button
is selected through this action, the collider region sends a
command to activate the corresponding action for the thyroid.
Four buttons, initially hidden and located on the right side of
the game home screen, will rotate 180 degrees around their

axis when activated. This action reveals new healthcare options
for the player’s thyroid character. These rotating buttons are
designed to be revealed to the player when certain health
conditions are met, enhancing the gameplay experience with
additional interactive elements. These buttons utilize the same
collider system for thyroid health maintenance, as shown in
Fig. 2, arranged from the top to the bottom right of the game
home screen. They represent mental health, thyroid hormone
replacement/antithyroid medication, radioactive iodine ther-
apy, and radiotherapy.
Each thyroid character is automatically customized when it
appears in the game home, reflecting its health profile, gender,
style, and age. A game’s system assigns accessories such
as hats, beads, ties, and glasses which totalize 60 available
adornments (Fig. 3), creating a unique visual identity that cor-
responds with the character’s individual attributes and health
status (Fig. 4). This automated customization adds depth to
the game, offering players a visual shorthand to understand
their character’s condition and history instantly. Specifically
designed animations showcase the consequences of player
actions on the virtual thyroid characters’ health, providing both
educational insight and interactive engagement.
Fig. 3. Customizable items we created for thyroid characters.
Fig. 4. Some thyroid characters randomly customized by the game system.
B. Gameplay
In our game, players have the opportunity to engage with
the virtual thyroid character through a variety of activities
designed to promote its well-being. These activities include:
• Sleeping: Ensure your virtual thyroid character gets
enough rest by putting it to sleep, which is fundamental
for its health and recovery (Fig. 5.a).
• Exercise: Engage your virtual thyroid character in phys-
ical activities to keep it fit and happy (Fig. 5.b).
• Care: Show care and attention to your virtual thyroid
character to boost its happiness and emotional well-being
(Fig. 5.c).
• Feeding: Provide your virtual thyroid character with
appropriate food to maintain its health and energy levels
(Fig. 6).
(a) Sleeping.
(b) Exercise.
(c) Care.
Fig. 5. Animations showing the actions for interacting with the virtual thyroid
character.
For nutrition, the game offers eight healthy food options
to nourish the thyroid character, thereby providing it with the
necessary energy throughout its existence. These food options
appear randomly within the gameplay model.
Among the implemented treatments are daily thyroid hor-
mone replacement medication to normalize hormone levels
and antihyroid medication, radioactive iodine therapy, radio-
therapy (Fig. 7), and monitoring of its mental health state.
We also introduced a spectrum of thyroid health states
ranging from hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism to can-
cerous tumors in various stages of progression, labeled as
phases 1 through 4 (Fig. 8). The character’s health fluctuates
among these states. A healthy condition potentially leads to
its demise either through natural lifespan or due to complex
health maintenance challenges.
On the screen, a single thyroid character is displayed at a
time, presenting a problem scenario for player analysis and
follow-up actions to preserve health. This includes personal
care actions, such as sleep, exercise, care, and nutrition (Figs.
5 and 6). These interactions mimic real-life pet care respon-
sibilities, translating them into a digital environment where
players can learn about and practice the essentials of virtual
thyroid management in a serious, yet fun and engaging way.
Using keyframes, all these game components were integrated
with Unity3D’s Animator to create a looping animation effect.
Additionally, we developed a life system that assigns a
health value displayed on a life bar for each thyroid character,

Fig. 6.
Animations depicting the consumption of various types of food to
energize the thyroid character.
located below it (Fig. 2). This system uses a specific formula
we devised to manage the thyroid health level (detailed in the
next section). The life system urges the player to stay vigilant
in caring for the virtual thyroid, as neglect can rapidly result
in the thyroid character’s termination.
The Sleep button activates a particle system to simulate
snoring and other soft sleeping sounds, depicted in our game
as “Zzz.” It also temporarily places a sleep mask on the thyroid
character for 8 seconds to simulate energy replenishment
during rest, without negatively affecting the thyroid’s health
bar. This design choice ensures that players who allow the
thyroid to rest are not penalized.
For the Care action, we employed a particle system that
bursts animated hearts to indicate the thyroid’s positive re-
sponse to the player’s care.
The Exercise feature includes three types of animations
where the thyroid character performs weight-lifting exercises
in up, down, or alternating motions. The speed and intensity
of these exercises adjust based on the thyroid’s current health
status, reflecting its physical condition at any game moment.
In the game, the thyroid’s physical capacity changes to reflect
its health status, impacting gameplay. Proper care maintains
thyroid health, while neglect can cause hormonal imbalances.
By pressing the Mental Health button, speech bubbles
appear on the screen with short narratives simulating a brief

(b) Mental health. This character is on post-surgical state.
(c) Radioactive iodine therapy and radiotherapy.

consultation with a psychologist, explaining potential issues
with the thyroid and the implications of worsening health,
including the development of nodules or cancer. This feature
enhances the game’s educational and interactive experience in
managing thyroid health.
A Radioactive Iodine Therapy button on the game home
screen can also be activated. The game animation mimics
real-life radioactive iodine therapy, administered orally to treat
thyroid conditions. A particle system replicates the radioactive
iodine’s administration with some special effects. Should ra-
dioactive iodine therapy prove ineffective for the presented
thyroid health case, the option for radiotherapy will become
available. The outcome of the treatment, such as the reduction
or disappearance of the nodule, depends on its size and type
of cancer. During radiotherapy, a new animation is triggered,
showing the thyroid character being fitted with a stabiliz-
ing mask for the radiotherapy session, with the animation’s
specifics varying based on the nodule’s current stage. This
interactive element was also originally designed to educate
players on thyroid cancer treatments and their strategies for
fighting the disease.
It is important to highlight that thyroid nodules may be

(b) Different tumor types and their regressions and evolutions.

located on the right, left, or both sides of the thyroid. Ad-
ditionally, the thyroid game character can represent a patient
who has undergone partial (in this case, only half a lobe will
be shown) or total thyroidectomy (here, the thyroid will be
visually absent, showing only the trachea). This feature aims
to educate players on the anatomical and surgical aspects of
thyroid health management.
If the thyroid character survives a predefined period in the
game, it will eventually die of age, akin to the original 1996
Tamagotchis. The character will go through a finite number
of iterations involving health care routines like sleeping,
exercising, eating, and mental health management. At the end
of these iterations, if the life bar remains above 50%, the game
background will fade, and the HUD buttons and life bar will
be disabled. A tombstone with either a happy or sad thyroid
angel will then appear, reflecting the care provided. After this,
the screen fades to the home screen where a new thyroid care
case begins. If the player opts to continue, the cycle restarts
with health care tailored to the new case.
C. Managing the Thyroid Health Level
At the start of a game session, one thyroid object is
instantiated randomly. A HUD, featuring a round-clock game
timer, is initialized at the top right corner of the game home
(Fig. 2). It fills up clockwise, completing upon the end of the
session with each thyroid character.
Every 0.5 seconds, the game calculates the life bar by
averaging sleep, exercise, care, and nutrition statuses, each
ranging from 0 to 1; additionally, every 0.1 seconds, it checks
for ongoing animations, disabling interaction buttons until
completion.
We define a formula for the thyroid character’s health level,
H, considering the provided percentages for initial thyroid
health problem deductions and the potential application of
treatment boosts. Each clinical case will represent different
health conditions and player action requirements.
The cumulative impact of multiple treatments applied in
response to various thyroid health conditions over time will
be observed based on player choices, reflecting the evolution
or regression of the character’s health conditions. These are
dynamically incorporated into the H formula, as the type of
illness may change over time (for example, a level 3 tumor
could evolve into a level 4 tumor, or a level 1 tumor could
regress to a cure). Thus, P Bi reflects the cumulative nature
of these positive interventions on the character’s health. Thus,
H is defined as follows:

D. Game Over Scene
In the game, a virtual thyroid character’s demise (Fig. 9)
can occur in several ways, each reflecting the level of care
they have received:
• Well-Cared-For, Natural Causes: A well-maintained
thyroid character may eventually pass away from old age,
simulating a life well-lived.
• Well-Cared-For,
Health
Complications: Even with
good care, a thyroid character can pass away due to
health-related issues, representing the complexities and
unpredictability of thyroid health conditions.

• Neglected, Due to Negligence: A thyroid character
that does not receive adequate care might deteriorate
due to neglect, highlighting the importance of consistent
attention.
• Neglected, Due to Abandonment: The most severe form
of neglect, where a thyroid character is left uncared for
and unattended, leading to their premature departure.
These outcomes encourage players to engage with the
game’s health management strategies and demonstrate the
consequences of their caregiving actions.

V. EXPERT MEDICAL GAMEPLAY EVALUATION
During this phase, our serious game underwent evaluation
by thyroid specialists. The specialists participated in testing
sessions, followed by completing a qualitative assessment
form. This form was essentially designed to capture their
insights regarding the game’s medical accuracy, effective-
ness, usability, and educational value. This process aimed to
identify strengths and areas for improvement, ensuring the
game captivates users while accurately conveying vital health
information.
A. Participants
Our team of three doctors, who are thyroid health specialists
and predominantly women, brings a collective experience of
12 to 23 years specifically in thyroid health to our user
testing sessions. Their diverse perspectives ensure thorough
evaluation and enhancement of our game’s educational content
and interactive features.
B. Methodology
During individual medical expert evaluations, we presented
six prerecorded game animations depicting thyroid clinical
cases, highlighting common scenarios in thyroid management.
These interactive animations allowed for decisions that influ-
enced outcomes, providing experts with detailed feedback on
prevalent conditions. This approach ensured comprehensive
yet manageable evaluations without overwhelming the testers.
The six cases were selected to represent a range of thyroid
conditions, including hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, thy-
roid cancer, nodules, and treatments such as radioactive iodine
and radiotherapy. These scenarios emphasized personalized
treatment plans and comprehensive care, focusing on medi-
cation regimens, patient care practices, psychological support,
and the importance of ongoing monitoring.
After viewing the animations, doctors completed a User
Experience form, collecting qualitative data on their experi-
ence with the game style, animation quality, clinical accuracy,
usability, art and design quality, engagement, educational
effectiveness, and empathy evocation. The form also gathered
feedback on the game’s strengths and weaknesses, providing
insights for further development.
C. Results and Analysis
The thyroid specialists offered valuable insights about our
game, and we integrated their responses. Based on their critical
feedback and observations, several comments were made and
enhancements were recommended for the game content as
follows.
“The six animations effectively depict various thyroid con-
ditions such as hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, and thyroid
cancer, providing a realistic portrayal of the symptoms and
effects on the thyroid gland. The clinical scenarios are compre-
hensive and accurately represent real-life situations faced by
individuals with thyroid conditions, offering valuable educa-
tional insights without inaccuracies or misleading information.
Game choice interactions are highly intuitive, complemented
by original and outstanding art and design quality. The visual
style effectively communicates serious medical information in
a captivating manner, keeping players from a wide age range
engaged throughout the user experience. The game effectively
educates about thyroid conditions while striking a balance
between education and entertainment. The comprehensive clin-
ical scenarios and treatment options are valuable for learning
about thyroid conditions and some of their possible manage-
ments, while gameplay animations capture attention and evoke
empathy”. Fig. 10 summarizes one key positive comment from
each thyroid specialist: accurate disease coverage, engaging
visuals, and a valuable learning tool.
Suggestions for improvement include incorporating more
diverse scenarios and treatment options, such as surgery, along
with corresponding interactive educational content. Addition-
ally, it was suggested that a feature to track player progress
in managing diverse thyroid conditions over time could also
enhance the overall learning evaluation. In particular, one
female thyroid specialist, who played Tamagotchi-style games
in childhood, reported feeling highly engaged with the game-
play animations, noting the game’s ability to capture attention
and feature “cute” visuals that enhance engagement and the
learning experience.
Further improvements to enhance the accuracy and edu-
cational impact of the game involve integrating additional
symptoms like insomnia and cautioning against vigorous ex-
ercise during severe hyperthyroidism. They also recommend
emphasizing the importance of a low-iodine diet within the
interactive narratives. Furthermore, underscore the favorable
prognosis and the predominant use of surgical intervention,

VI. CONCLUSIONS AND FUTURE WORK
Developing CancerST, a serious game for thyroid cancer
education, allows us to explore innovative approaches and
contribute to the field. This Tamagotchi-style game pro-
motes cross-disciplinary collaboration across computing, de-
sign, healthcare, and education, enhancing innovation at the
nexus of technology and health. By engaging players in
managing the health of a thyroid virtual pet, the game can
provide valuable insights into user interaction with health
management tasks.
Thyroid specialists have praised the game for its engaging
visuals, accurate portrayal of thyroid diseases, and educational
value. Their evaluations highlight that the animations real-
istically depict thyroid conditions and the clinical scenarios
provide comprehensive educational insights. With intuitive
interactions and high-quality art, the game effectively com-
municates medical information, as suggested by professionals.
This aligns with our goal of using interactive technology to
enhance health education and patient engagement in thyroid
health management.
In future work, we plan to incorporate thyroid surgery
animations, treatments, and interactive educational content.
Expert medical input will enhance targeting for those with
thyroid issues, thereby increasing the game’s value. This
feedback is essential for refining the game to better meet the
needs of patients and healthcare professionals. Tracking player
progress, featuring symptoms like insomnia, emphasizing a
low-iodine diet, and highlighting surgical treatments and ra-
dioactive iodine for severe cases will improve learning assess-
ment. Finally, adding a positive message at the game’s end
could underscore the effectiveness of early cancer treatment.
